The tracking volume is closed by calorimeter walls of 1940 polystyrene-based plastic scintillator blocks, about 10 cm thick, each coupled, mostly through a light guide, to a low-radioactivity 3-in. or 5-in. photomultiplier.
The calorimeter reaches an energy resolution of 14-17% FWHM for 1 MeV electrons and a time resolution of about 250 ps at 1 MeV.
Iron, water and wood shielding surround the detector, which sits under about 4800 m water equivalent of rock.
The follow-up detector will hold about 100 kg of isotope in the same tracker-calorimeter layout and aims at a half-life sensitivity near 1e26 years.
It requires an energy resolution of about 8% FWHM for 1 MeV electrons in every calorimeter cell.
It requires a time resolution of about 400 ps at 1 MeV between two cells, to reject electrons crossing the detector from outside.
Each electron of a decay must have its energy measured individually, and all calorimeter materials must keep 208Tl and 214Bi activity low enough for a 3 MeV region of interest.

The following describes a particle-physics detector.

A liquid-scintillator neutrino detector sits in a deep underground laboratory (about 3800 m water equivalent). Its target is about 278 t of an aromatic hydrocarbon scintillator (trimethylbenzene with a fluor), held in a 4.25 m-radius thin nylon vessel. An inert hydrocarbon buffer surrounds the vessel inside a 6.85 m-radius stainless-steel sphere that carries about 2200 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The light yield is about 500 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution about 5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution about 12 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold about 0.2 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g.
The detector measures sub-MeV solar neutrinos through neutrino-electron elastic scattering. It detects electron antineutrinos through inverse beta decay on free protons: a prompt positron followed by a neutron capture about 250 us later.
A shielded access pit lies beneath the water tank, about 8.25 m from the detector centre.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in the access pit.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target must stay as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

A liquid-scintillator neutrino detector sits in a deep underground laboratory (about 3800 m water equivalent). Its target is about 278 t of an aromatic hydrocarbon scintillator (trimethylbenzene with a fluor), held in a 4.25 m-radius thin nylon vessel. An inert hydrocarbon buffer surrounds the vessel inside a 6.85 m-radius stainless-steel sphere that carries about 2200 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The light yield is about 500 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution about 5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution about 12 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold about 0.2 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g.
The detector measures sub-MeV solar neutrinos through neutrino-electron elastic scattering. It detects electron antineutrinos through inverse beta decay on free protons: a prompt positron followed by a neutron capture about 250 us later.
A shielded access pit lies beneath the water tank, about 8.25 m from the detector centre.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in the access pit.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target must stay as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

An inert hydrocarbon buffer surrounds the vessel inside a 6.85 m-radius stainless-steel sphere that carries about 2200 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The light yield is about 500 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution about 5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution about 12 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold about 0.2 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g.
The detector measures sub-MeV solar neutrinos through neutrino-electron elastic scattering. It detects electron antineutrinos through inverse beta decay on free protons: a prompt positron followed by a neutron capture about 250 us later.
A shielded access pit lies beneath the water tank, about 8.25 m from the detector centre.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in the access pit.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target must stay as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

The detector measures sub-MeV solar neutrinos through neutrino-electron elastic scattering. It detects electron antineutrinos through inverse beta decay on free protons: a prompt positron followed by a neutron capture about 250 us later.

For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.

A liquid-scintillator neutrino detector sits in an underground laboratory at about 3100 m water equivalent. Its target is linear alkylbenzene scintillator with a fluor, filling a 4.6 m-radius transparent membrane vessel. The scintillator solvent is ordinary alkylbenzene with natural hydrogen, about 6e28 hydrogen atoms and 2.9e29 electrons per cubic metre.
The light yield is 450 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution 5.5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution 14 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold 0.25 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g. In the 0.25-0.6 MeV window, the fiducial volume (radius 3.4 m, 165 m3) records about 100 background events per day, mostly from solar neutrinos.

Its target is linear alkylbenzene scintillator with a fluor, filling a 4.6 m-radius transparent membrane vessel. An inert buffer liquid surrounds the vessel inside a 7.2 m-radius steel sphere that carries 2500 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The scintillator solvent is ordinary alkylbenzene with natural hydrogen, about 6e28 hydrogen atoms and 2.9e29 electrons per cubic metre.
The light yield is 450 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution 5.5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution 14 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold 0.25 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g. In the 0.25-0.6 MeV window, the fiducial volume (radius 3.4 m, 165 m3) records about 100 background events per day, mostly from solar neutrinos.
The physics programme is low-energy solar neutrinos (7Be, pep, CNO and 8B), with event-by-event neutron detection by capture gammas.
A shielded access chamber, 1 m across, lies beneath the detector with its centre 7.5 m from the detector centre. It holds up to 2.5 t of emitter plus shielding.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in that chamber.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target liquid stays as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

Its target is linear alkylbenzene scintillator with a fluor, filling a 4.6 m-radius transparent membrane vessel. The scintillator solvent is ordinary alkylbenzene with natural hydrogen, about 6e28 hydrogen atoms and 2.9e29 electrons per cubic metre.
The light yield is 450 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution 5.5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution 14 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold 0.25 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g. In the 0.25-0.6 MeV window, the fiducial volume (radius 3.4 m, 165 m3) records about 100 background events per day, mostly from solar neutrinos.
The physics programme is low-energy solar neutrinos (7Be, pep, CNO and 8B), with event-by-event neutron detection by capture gammas.
A shielded access chamber, 1 m across, lies beneath the detector with its centre 7.5 m from the detector centre. It holds up to 2.5 t of emitter plus shielding.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in that chamber.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target liquid stays as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

A liquid-scintillator neutrino detector sits in an underground laboratory at about 3100 m water equivalent. Its target is linear alkylbenzene scintillator with a fluor, filling a 4.6 m-radius transparent membrane vessel. An inert buffer liquid surrounds the vessel inside a 7.2 m-radius steel sphere that carries 2500 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The scintillator solvent is ordinary alkylbenzene with natural hydrogen, about 6e28 hydrogen atoms and 2.9e29 electrons per cubic metre.
The light yield is 450 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution 5.5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution 14 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold 0.25 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g. In the 0.25-0.6 MeV window, the fiducial volume (radius 3.4 m, 165 m3) records about 100 background events per day, mostly from solar neutrinos.
The physics programme is low-energy solar neutrinos (7Be, pep, CNO and 8B), with event-by-event neutron detection by capture gammas.
A shielded access chamber, 1 m across, lies beneath the detector with its centre 7.5 m from the detector centre. It holds up to 2.5 t of emitter plus shielding.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in that chamber.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target liquid stays as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

An inert buffer liquid surrounds the vessel inside a 7.2 m-radius steel sphere that carries 2500 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The scintillator solvent is ordinary alkylbenzene with natural hydrogen, about 6e28 hydrogen atoms and 2.9e29 electrons per cubic metre.
The light yield is 450 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution 5.5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution 14 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold 0.25 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g. In the 0.25-0.6 MeV window, the fiducial volume (radius 3.4 m, 165 m3) records about 100 background events per day, mostly from solar neutrinos.
The physics programme is low-energy solar neutrinos (7Be, pep, CNO and 8B), with event-by-event neutron detection by capture gammas.
A shielded access chamber, 1 m across, lies beneath the detector with its centre 7.5 m from the detector centre. It holds up to 2.5 t of emitter plus shielding.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in that chamber.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target liquid stays as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

A liquid-scintillator neutrino detector sits in an underground laboratory at about 3100 m water equivalent. Its target is linear alkylbenzene scintillator with a fluor, filling a 4.6 m-radius transparent membrane vessel. An inert buffer liquid surrounds the vessel inside a 7.2 m-radius steel sphere that carries 2500 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The scintillator solvent is ordinary alkylbenzene with natural hydrogen, about 6e28 hydrogen atoms and 2.9e29 electrons per cubic metre.
The light yield is 450 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution 5.5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution 14 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold 0.25 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g. In the 0.25-0.6 MeV window, the fiducial volume (radius 3.4 m, 165 m3) records about 100 background events per day, mostly from solar neutrinos.
The physics programme is low-energy solar neutrinos (7Be, pep, CNO and 8B), with event-by-event neutron detection by capture gammas.
A shielded access chamber, 1 m across, lies beneath the detector with its centre 7.5 m from the detector centre. It holds up to 2.5 t of emitter plus shielding.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in that chamber.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target liquid stays as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

A liquid-scintillator neutrino detector sits in an underground laboratory at about 3100 m water equivalent. Its target is linear alkylbenzene scintillator with a fluor, filling a 4.6 m-radius transparent membrane vessel. An inert buffer liquid surrounds the vessel inside a 7.2 m-radius steel sphere that carries 2500 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The scintillator solvent is fully deuterated alkylbenzene: 99.8% of the hydrogen sites carry deuterium, which leaves about 1.2e26 hydrogen-1 atoms, 6e28 deuterium atoms and 2.9e29 electrons per cubic metre. The neutral-current measurement of 8B solar neutrinos on deuterium relies on this.
The light yield is 450 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution 5.5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution 14 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold 0.25 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g. In the 0.25-0.6 MeV window, the fiducial volume (radius 3.4 m, 165 m3) records about 100 background events per day, mostly from solar neutrinos.
The physics programme is low-energy solar neutrinos (7Be, pep, CNO and 8B), with event-by-event neutron detection by capture gammas.
A shielded access chamber, 1 m across, lies beneath the detector with its centre 7.5 m from the detector centre. It holds up to 2.5 t of emitter plus shielding.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in that chamber.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target liquid stays as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

A liquid-scintillator neutrino detector sits in an underground laboratory at about 3100 m water equivalent. Its target is linear alkylbenzene scintillator with a fluor, filling a 4.6 m-radius transparent membrane vessel. An inert buffer liquid surrounds the vessel inside a 7.2 m-radius steel sphere that carries 2500 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The scintillator solvent is fully deuterated alkylbenzene: 99.8% of the hydrogen sites carry deuterium, which leaves about 1.2e26 hydrogen-1 atoms, 6e28 deuterium atoms and 2.9e29 electrons per cubic metre. The neutral-current measurement of 8B solar neutrinos on deuterium relies on this.
The light yield is 450 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution 5.5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution 14 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold 0.25 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g. In the 0.25-0.6 MeV window, the fiducial volume (radius 3.4 m, 165 m3) records about 100 background events per day, mostly from solar neutrinos.
The physics programme is low-energy solar neutrinos (7Be, pep, CNO and 8B), with event-by-event neutron detection by capture gammas.
A shielded access chamber, 1 m across, lies beneath the detector with its centre 7.5 m from the detector centre. It holds up to 2.5 t of emitter plus shielding.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in that chamber.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target liquid stays as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

The following describes a particle-physics detector.

Borexino is a liquid-scintillator neutrino detector in the Gran Sasso underground laboratory (about 3800 m water equivalent). Its target is about 278 t of pseudocumene with PPO, held in a 4.25 m-radius nylon vessel. A pseudocumene buffer surrounds the vessel inside a 6.85 m-radius stainless-steel sphere that carries about 2200 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The light yield is about 500 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution about 5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution about 12 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold about 0.2 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g.
The detector measures sub-MeV solar neutrinos through neutrino-electron elastic scattering. It detects electron antineutrinos through inverse beta decay on free protons: a prompt positron followed by a neutron capture about 250 us later.
A shielded access pit lies beneath the water tank, about 8.25 m from the detector centre.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in the access pit.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target must stay as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

Its target is about 278 t of pseudocumene with PPO, held in a 4.25 m-radius nylon vessel. A pseudocumene buffer surrounds the vessel inside a 6.85 m-radius stainless-steel sphere that carries about 2200 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The light yield is about 500 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution about 5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution about 12 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold about 0.2 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g.
The detector measures sub-MeV solar neutrinos through neutrino-electron elastic scattering. It detects electron antineutrinos through inverse beta decay on free protons: a prompt positron followed by a neutron capture about 250 us later.
A shielded access pit lies beneath the water tank, about 8.25 m from the detector centre.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in the access pit.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target must stay as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

Borexino is a liquid-scintillator neutrino detector in the Gran Sasso underground laboratory (about 3800 m water equivalent). Its target is about 278 t of pseudocumene with PPO, held in a 4.25 m-radius nylon vessel. A pseudocumene buffer surrounds the vessel inside a 6.85 m-radius stainless-steel sphere that carries about 2200 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The light yield is about 500 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution about 5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution about 12 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold about 0.2 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g.
The detector measures sub-MeV solar neutrinos through neutrino-electron elastic scattering. It detects electron antineutrinos through inverse beta decay on free protons: a prompt positron followed by a neutron capture about 250 us later.
A shielded access pit lies beneath the water tank, about 8.25 m from the detector centre.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in the access pit.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target must stay as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

A pseudocumene buffer surrounds the vessel inside a 6.85 m-radius stainless-steel sphere that carries about 2200 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The light yield is about 500 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution about 5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution about 12 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold about 0.2 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g.
The detector measures sub-MeV solar neutrinos through neutrino-electron elastic scattering. It detects electron antineutrinos through inverse beta decay on free protons: a prompt positron followed by a neutron capture about 250 us later.
A shielded access pit lies beneath the water tank, about 8.25 m from the detector centre.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in the access pit.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target must stay as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

Its target is about 278 t of pseudocumene with PPO, held in a 4.25 m-radius nylon vessel. A pseudocumene buffer surrounds the vessel inside a 6.85 m-radius stainless-steel sphere that carries about 2200 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The light yield is about 500 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution about 5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution about 12 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold about 0.2 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g.
The detector measures sub-MeV solar neutrinos through neutrino-electron elastic scattering. It detects electron antineutrinos through inverse beta decay on free protons: a prompt positron followed by a neutron capture about 250 us later.
A shielded access pit lies beneath the water tank, about 8.25 m from the detector centre.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in the access pit.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target must stay as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.

Borexino is a liquid-scintillator neutrino detector in the Gran Sasso underground laboratory (about 3800 m water equivalent). Its target is about 278 t of pseudocumene with PPO, held in a 4.25 m-radius nylon vessel. A pseudocumene buffer surrounds the vessel inside a 6.85 m-radius stainless-steel sphere that carries about 2200 photomultipliers. A water Cherenkov muon veto encloses the sphere.
The light yield is about 500 photoelectrons per MeV, the energy resolution about 5% at 1 MeV, the vertex resolution about 12 cm at 1 MeV, and the analysis threshold about 0.2 MeV. Uranium and thorium contamination is below 1e-17 g/g.
The detector measures sub-MeV solar neutrinos through neutrino-electron elastic scattering. It detects electron antineutrinos through inverse beta decay on free protons: a prompt positron followed by a neutron capture about 250 us later.
A shielded access pit lies beneath the water tank, about 8.25 m from the detector centre.
The collaboration now wants to test for oscillation into a sterile state with a mass splitting near 1 eV2, using an intense artificial neutrino emitter placed in the access pit.
The test requires at least 1500 source-induced interactions in the fiducial volume within 18 months of data.
For at least 80% of those interactions, the neutrino energy must be known to within 10%, so that the oscillation pattern can be traced in distance over energy.
Over the counting period chosen for the analysis, source-induced interactions in the selected energy window must outnumber background events in that window.
The target must stay as it is, because the solar-neutrino programme continues.
